question.:question/problem:
Use the substitution $u=2^{x} + 2$. Which integral is obtained?

$$
\int 3 \cdot 2^{x} \left(2^{x} + 2\right)^{3}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=2^{x} + 2$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(2^{x} \ln{\left(2 \right)})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Work where $2^{x} + 2>0$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int 3 \cdot 2^{x} \left(2^{x} + 2\right)^{3}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}\left(\int u^{3}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

The transformed integral is

$$
\frac{3}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}\left(\int u^{3}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=- 2 x + e^{2 x} + 1$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(2 e^{2 x} - 2)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Use a connected real interval on which the integrand is defined.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4 e^{2 x} - 4}{- 2 x + e^{2 x} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\ln\left|u\right|\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2\left(\ln\left|- 2 x + e^{2 x} + 1\right|\right)+C.
$$
